RE-STAMPED AGAINST A COMMIT THAT EXISTS, WHICH IS WHAT THIS FLOOR NEEDED. It was UNCHECKED, not merely orphaned: its stamp f5ed0acf783 could not be resolved by 'git cat-file' at all, so no ancestry test could even fail honestly. CLAUDE.md section 4 records how that happened -- an earlier rebase banked it at its own intermediate onto-tip and the replay then rewrote that commit away -- and says the work is a re-stamp against a resolvable commit rather than a re-measure.

Measured anyway, because a stamp is a claim about a tree and this one had never been checkable. Summing the three service-worker programs as the workflow does, 'npx tsc --project tsconfig.serviceworker.<lane>.json --noEmit' counted by 'grep -c "error TS"': web 48, pos 3, event 33, total 84. The floor said 85, and CLAUDE.md records the composition behind it as 49 + 3 + 33, so the single line that moved is in the web program.

Upstream's, not ours: at the rebase's onto-tip a1ba7203ac3 the same three programs also read 48 / 3 / 33. None of our 57 commits touched it.

Measured at 6011a0335cc in a clean detached worktree with node_modules symlinked in, since a worktree carries none.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

Conflict during the 2026-09-03 rebase of 19.0-marin onto origin, between this floor's 85 (stamped afc037e38ca) and 91cda83aa90's own recorded 84 (stamped 62197c60c7f, moved by 'the service-worker rewrite in the JS commit'). That JS commit is 9a1bd99fca20, which touches addons/mail/static/src/service_worker.js and has not landed in this tree yet at 91cda83aa90's position in the replayed sequence -- it is still later in the rebase todo. Re-measured live at f5ed0acf783 (this commit's onto tip): npx tsc --project tsconfig.serviceworker.<lane>.json --noEmit over web, pos, event, summed -- 49 + 3 + 33 = 85, unchanged from the floor. So 91cda83aa90 does not itself move this count; the 84 belongs to 9a1bd99fca20's own rebase step, to be banked there once that commit is replayed and re-measured against its own resulting tree.
